question: Abibsi vs. Nolan: Set 1 Games O/U 8.5
description:
This market refers to the tennis match between Mohamed Ali Abibsi and William Nolan in the M15 Monastir, originally scheduled for September 15, 2026 at 4:30AM ET.
This market will resolve to "Over" if the total number of games completed in the first set equals or exceeds 9. Otherwise, it will resolve to "Under." Any first-set tiebreak counts as one (1) game.
If the match is postponed or suspended, this market will remain open until the first set has been completed. A postponement alone will not trigger a 50-50 resolution.
If the match is permanently abandoned before the first set is completed, or if the first set has not been completed by September 29, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve 50-50, unless the outcome has already been unconditionally determined based on completed play. An outcome is considered determined if it would have been guaranteed had the set been played to completion using the minimum number of additional games required. For example, for a line of 9.5, if play stops with the first set at 5-4, completing the set would have required at least 1 additional game, resulting in at least 10 games played, so "Over" would resolve as the winning outcome.
The primary resolution source for this market will be official ITF statistics; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: M15 Monastir: Mohamed Ali Abibsi vs William Nolan
events.description:
This market refers to the tennis match between Mohamed Ali Abibsi and William Nolan in the M15 Monastir, Qualifying, originally scheduled for September 15, 2026 at 4:30AM ET.

This market will resolve to 'Mohamed Ali Abibsi' if Mohamed Ali Abibsi advances against William Nolan.

This market will resolve to 'William Nolan' if William Nolan advances against Mohamed Ali Abibsi.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or a winner has not been determined by September 29, 2026, 11:59 PM ET (14 days after the scheduled start), this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match begins but is not completed, and one player advances due to the opponent's retirement, default, or disqualification, this market will resolve to the player who advances.

If the match ends in a walkover (player withdraws before the start and the other advances automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the International Tennis Federation (ITF). A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
